 It's almost time for most Americans to set their clocks back an hour. Daylight saving time ends in the U.S. at 2 a.m. local time next Sunday. Standard time will last until March 14, when we will again “spring forward” with the return of daylight saving time. Most countries do not observe daylight saving time. For those that do — mostly in North America and Europe — the date that clocks are changed varies. In the U.S., Hawaii and most of Arizona don’t change and stay on standard time.

 An extra hour of sleep is on the way for most Americans, though the “fall back” to standard time will bring darker afternoons, too.
 One tip: Try to get outside for some morning sun — it’ll help your body clock reset faster.
